sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A phone plan costs $8 plus $4 per gigabyte of data. The bill was $24. Which equation represents the number of gigabytes, x?
A bike rental costs $29 plus $12 per hour. If the total cost was $98, how many hours, x, were rented?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student solves 3x - 5 = 34. They write 3x = 39, then say x = 39. Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The student subtracted incorrectly; the correct solution is x = 29/3.
The student should have multiplied by 3 instead of dividing; x = 117.
The student forgot to divide both sides by 3; the correct solution is x = 13.

items.prompt: A student says -x + 20 = -x + 20 has one solution because they can solve for x. Which statement correctly analyzes the equation?
choices: The equation has exactly one solution, found by dividing both sides by the coefficient of x.
The equation cannot be classified without graphing it.
The equation has infinitely many solutions; both sides are identical for every x.
The equation has no solution; simplifying gives 20 = 20, which is never true.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
